media_work.title: 60 Minutes
media_work.focus_or_theme: False confessions, police interrogation techniques, juvenile suspects, wrongful convictions in Chicago.
media_work.summaryNotes: Chicago identified as having a high number of documented false confession cases ("False Confession Capital").

media_item.item_title: Segment "The False Confession Capital" (Reported by Byron Pitts)
media_item.focus_or_theme: False confessions, police interrogation techniques, juvenile suspects, wrongful convictions in Chicago.
key_quotes_raw: Interviews with exonerated individuals describing interrogation experiences; Psychologist Saul Kassin explaining the psychology of false confessions; Cook County State's Attorney Anita Alvarez defending police actions at the time.
systemic_issues_raw: Psychological vulnerability of suspects (especially juveniles) during intense interrogation, police tactics leading to false confessions, reliance on confessions over contradictory evidence (like DNA), difficulty in overturning convictions based on confessions.
policy_recommendations_raw: Implied need for reforms in police interrogation practices (e.g., recording interrogations, time limits, special protections for juveniles), better evaluation of confession evidence by prosecutors and courts.

contributing_factors_raw: Coerced false confession, lengthy interrogation (12+ hours), juvenile suspect (17), alleged police pressure/feeding details.
featured_individuals.status_raw: Exonerated (Certificate of Innocence); pursued civil rights lawsuit.
organizations_involved_raw: People's Law Office, MacArthur Justice Center, Northwestern University School of Law, Innocence Project.
